problem: Return a minimum-total-integer-weight path from node 0 to node n-1 in a small numbered DAG.
goal: Feasibility and global optimality on the original graph; a cheaper-looking path in a modified graph does not solve this goal.
scope: Purpose-built public graphs, 2 to 12 nodes, unique directed edges u < v; generated evaluation cases have every node reachable from source.
reference: Separately authored exhaustive path enumeration without pruning.
practical_baseline: Direct topological shortest-path dynamic program; exhaustive enumeration is a cross-check, not the only efficiency baseline.
acceptance_criterion: A candidate accepted as optimal by all_edges_certificate must have reference regret zero. Invalid certificates cannot by themselves establish algorithm suboptimality.
cost_policy: Report validation edge scans, adjacency indexing, solver edge visits, witness edge visits, verifier edge checks and reference edge visits separately. No wall-time, token, learned-controller or equal-total-budget performance claim.
stop_rule: Keep all counterexamples; repair a demonstrated verification defect, test old and new cases, and stop at a scoped result. Do not infer general research effectiveness or continue tuning the goal.
exposure: All cases are public development/regression inputs, not a hidden or independent final holdout. No private problem text is included.
